Cartier.name: Santos de Cartier
Cartier.desc: A square watch with exposed screws on the bezel, first made for a pilot in 1904, with a quick-swap bracelet.

Cartier.name: Tank Must
Cartier.desc: The cheapest way into Cartier's classic rectangular Tank, with a light-powered version that needs no battery changes.

Cartier.name: Tank Louis Cartier
Cartier.desc: The original gold Tank shape from 1922, thin and elegant, often called the most classic dress watch there is.

Cartier.name: Ballon Bleu de Cartier
Cartier.desc: A round, pebble-like case with the crown tucked under a blue stone guard, popular as an everyday luxury watch.

Cartier.name: Panthère de Cartier
Cartier.desc: A small square watch on a supple brick-style bracelet that feels like jewellery and is worn mostly by women.

Cartier.name: Pasha de Cartier
Cartier.desc: A round watch with a chained crown cover and square minute track, with quick-change straps and bracelets.

Zenith.name: Chronomaster Sport
Zenith.desc: A steel sports chronograph whose fast movement can time events to a tenth of a second, at a fair price for its class.

Zenith.name: Defy Skyline
Zenith.desc: A sporty steel watch with a built-in bracelet, an angular bezel and a star-patterned dial.

Zenith.name: Chronomaster Original
Zenith.desc: A faithful remake of the 1969 El Primero chronograph with its famous three different coloured sub-dials.

Zenith.name: Pilot
Zenith.desc: A modern pilot's watch with big numerals and a date, offered in steel or black ceramic.

Zenith.name: Chronomaster Solo Sport
Zenith.desc: A new 2026 three-hand version of the Chronomaster Sport, keeping the look without the stopwatch.

Zenith.name: Defy Extreme
Zenith.desc: A big, bold titanium chronograph with swappable straps, aimed at buyers who want a statement watch.

Jaeger-LeCoultre.name: Reverso
Jaeger-LeCoultre.desc: An Art Deco rectangular watch whose case flips over to protect the glass, first made for polo players in 1931.

Jaeger-LeCoultre.name: Master Control
Jaeger-LeCoultre.desc: A simple, well-made round dress watch with a date, tested for 1,000 hours before it leaves the factory.

Jaeger-LeCoultre.name: Polaris
Jaeger-LeCoultre.desc: A sporty steel watch inspired by a 1968 alarm diver, with a rotating inner ring and a matching bracelet.

Jaeger-LeCoultre.name: Master Ultra Thin
Jaeger-LeCoultre.desc: A very thin, classic round watch, including a well-known moon phase model, meant to slide under a shirt cuff.

Jaeger-LeCoultre.name: Rendez-Vous
Jaeger-LeCoultre.desc: A feminine round watch with ornate numerals and a floral feel, the brand's main women's line.

Glashütte Original.name: Seventies Chronograph Panorama Date
Glashütte Original.desc: A cushion-shaped 1970s-style chronograph with a big date display, made in Germany's watch town of Glashütte.

Glashütte Original.name: SeaQ
Glashütte Original.desc: A vintage-style dive watch based on the brand's 1969 Spezimatic diver, rated to 200 metres.

Glashütte Original.name: Senator Excellence
Glashütte Original.desc: A classic round dress watch with a long 100-hour power reserve and finely finished German movement.

Glashütte Original.name: PanoMaticLunar
Glashütte Original.desc: The brand's signature off-centre dial with a big date and moon phase, unlike any Swiss design.

Glashütte Original.name: Sixties
Glashütte Original.desc: The cheapest Glashütte Original, a 1960s-style round watch with domed, often gradient coloured dials.

Grand Seiko mechanical.name: Heritage Collection Hi-Beat
Grand Seiko mechanical.desc: Crisp, angular steel watches based on 1960s Grand Seiko designs, known for flawless polishing and detailed textured dials.

Grand Seiko mechanical.name: Evolution 9
Grand Seiko mechanical.desc: A modern take on the house style with wider hands, an 80-hour power reserve and birch bark textured dials.

Grand Seiko mechanical.name: Elegance
Grand Seiko mechanical.desc: Gentle, classic dress watches including a hand-wound model, generally the quietest designs in the range.

Grand Seiko mechanical.name: Sport Collection
Grand Seiko mechanical.desc: Tough, larger dive and GMT watches with the same fine finishing, built for daily hard use.

The Citizen mechanical.name: Caliber 0200
The Citizen mechanical.desc: Citizen's top mechanical watch, with a finely finished in-house movement and a crisp dial, a value rival to Grand Seiko.

The Citizen mechanical.name: Caliber 0210 (Caliber 0200 open-heart)
The Citizen mechanical.desc: The same watch with a cut-out on the dial so you can see the movement's beating balance wheel.

The Citizen mechanical.name: Caliber 0270
The Citizen mechanical.desc: A high-precision mechanical model sold mainly in Japan, aimed at accuracy collectors.

Horage.name: Supersede
Horage.desc: An integrated-bracelet sports watch with Horage's own slim micro-rotor movement, sold in date and GMT versions.

Horage.name: Autark
Horage.desc: The brand's original everyday steel watch, offering an in-house Swiss movement at a modest price.

Horage.name: Lensman
Horage.desc: Titanium watches styled after vintage camera lenses, from simple models to a tourbillon.

Horage.name: Tourbillon
Horage.desc: One of the cheapest Swiss tourbillons, a spinning cage movement normally reserved for luxury brands.

Louis Erard.name: Excellence Régulateur
Louis Erard.desc: A watch that shows hours, minutes and seconds on separate dials, a classic old clockmaker layout.

Louis Erard.name: Le Régulateur
Louis Erard.desc: Regulator-dial watches made with famous designers like Alain Silberstein and Konstantin Chaykin, often in limited runs.

Louis Erard.name: Excellence Petite Seconde
Louis Erard.desc: An affordable Swiss dress watch with a small seconds dial and enamel or guilloché options.

Louis Erard.name: Excellence Guilloché Main
Louis Erard.desc: Classic dress watches with patterned dials hand-cut on old engine-turning machines.

Louis Erard.name: La Semaine
Louis Erard.desc: A playful collaboration piece that shows the day of the week with a big hand.

Sartory Billard.name: SB04
Sartory Billard.desc: A simple, sporty French-designed watch built with independent-brand finishing at a modest price.

Sartory Billard.name: SB05
Sartory Billard.desc: A refined made-to-order dress watch with many dial and finishing choices, from hammered to lacquer.

Sartory Billard.name: SB01
Sartory Billard.desc: The brand's first watch, a three-hand design made to customer order.

Habring².name: Felix
Habring².desc: A plain, honest Austrian dress watch with the brand's own movement, made by a husband and wife team.

Habring².name: Erwin
Habring².desc: The Felix with a seconds hand that jumps once a second like a quartz clock, but done mechanically.

Habring².name: Foudroyante-Felix
Habring².desc: Adds a tiny dial that spins through eighths of a second, a rare old complication at an approachable price.

Habring².name: Doppel-Felix
Habring².desc: A split-seconds chronograph that can time two events at once, made by the man who designed IWC's famous one.

Habring².name: Chrono-Felix
Habring².desc: A one-button chronograph with the brand's own movement, including a perpetual calendar version.

Kudoke.name: Kudoke 2
Kudoke.movement: Hand-wound, modified base with hand-engraved bridges
Kudoke.desc: A hand-engraved German watch with a day and night indicator that shows a sun and moon, a cult favourite.

Kudoke.name: Kudoke 3
Kudoke.desc: A simpler, cleaner three-hand Kudoke with hand-engraved details and colourful dial options.

Kudoke.name: Kudoke 1
Kudoke.desc: The entry Kudoke, a small-seconds watch with hand-engraved movement and a clean dial.

Kudoke.name: Kudoke ∞
Kudoke.desc: A higher-end piece with a sculpted engraved movement visible from the front.

Lundis Bleus.name: Ref. 1100
Lundis Bleus.desc: The founding model of a small Swiss workshop, a clean three-hand dress watch with an in-house case.

Lundis Bleus.name: Ref. 1120 Contemporaines
Lundis Bleus.desc: Dress watches with stone, enamel or mother-of-pearl dials, made by hand in the brand's own workshop.

Lundis Bleus.name: Ref. 1120 Métiers d'Art
Lundis Bleus.desc: Hand-made artistic dials using enamel, mosaic or engraving, rare at this price.

Lundis Bleus.name: Ref. 1110
Lundis Bleus.desc: A kiln-fired enamel dial watch in deep colours, shortlisted at the Geneva watch awards.

Laine.name: V38
Laine.desc: A slim, refined dress watch with hand-made guilloché dial options, from a Finnish maker working in Switzerland.

Laine.name: P37
Laine.desc: A smaller hand-wound dress watch with bold dial colours, sold in numbered editions.

Laine.name: P33
Laine.desc: A new 2026 compact model for smaller wrists, made in the same craft-focused way.

Dornblüth & Sohn.desc: A clean German hand-wound watch with a large small-seconds dial and a broad, traditional movement.
The simplest Dornblüth, a plain time-only watch built with old-school German craftsmanship.

Dornblüth & Sohn.name: Quintus
Dornblüth & Sohn.desc: A regulator-style watch with separate hours and minutes, and movement parts made almost entirely in-house.
Adds a power reserve indicator so you can see when the watch needs winding.

Felipe Pikullik.name: Mondphase 1
Felipe Pikullik.movement: Hand-wound, modified base with moon phase
Felipe Pikullik.desc: A small-batch Berlin-made watch with a precise moon phase, now in its final meteorite dial run.

Felipe Pikullik.name: Mondphase II
Felipe Pikullik.desc: The brand's first fully in-house movement, a moon phase watch made in 20 pieces per metal.

Otsuka Lotec.name: No.6
Otsuka Lotec.movement: Automatic, Miyota base with in-house retrograde module
Otsuka Lotec.desc: A retrograde-display watch inspired by an old air pressure gauge, built by a one-man Tokyo workshop.

Otsuka Lotec.name: No.7.5
Otsuka Lotec.movement: Automatic, Miyota 82S5 with in-house jumping hour
Otsuka Lotec.desc: A jumping-hour watch styled like a vintage 8mm movie camera lens, rarely sold outside Japan.

Otsuka Lotec.name: No.8
Otsuka Lotec.movement: Automatic, Miyota base with in-house module
Otsuka Lotec.desc: Shows jumping hours and backward-jumping minutes, inspired by studio mixing consoles, sold by lottery.
